Start from each `protein` record; combine it with each `Institution` record for which Institution id (`Institution.Institution_id`) equals Institution id (`protein.Institution_id`) (compared as text, character by character), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); group the kept records by athletic conference (`Institution.Primary_Conference`); each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) athletic conference (`Institution.Primary_Conference`); (2) the number of records in the group.
Step 2. Start from the rows of step 1; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the sum of column (2) of step 1 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 3. Start from the rows of step 1; combine it with the rows of step 2 for which it is not true that column (1) of step 2 is missing, one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 1; (2) column (2) of step 1; (3) A ÷ B. Here A is column (2) of step 1; B is column (1) of step 2.
Step 4. Start from the rows of step 3; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the average of column (3) of step 3 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 5 (the answer). Start from the rows of step 3; combine it with the rows of step 4 for which it is not true that column (1) of step 4 is missing, one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); keep only the records for which column (3) of step 3 is greater than column (1) of step 4; for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 3; (2) column (2) of step 3; (3) column (3) of step 3; (4) A − B. Here A is column (3) of step 3; B is column (1) of step 4.

why: share of the all total of number of protein records (all level)
gap to the all average of number of protein records: share of the all total (all level)
coarsen to all: SUM (additive), AVG (averaged), AVG (averaged)
examples.sql: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "Institution"."Primary_Conference" AS g, COUNT(*) AS m1 FROM "protein" JOIN "Institution" ON "Institution"."Institution_id" = "protein"."Institution_id" GROUP BY "Institution"."Primary_Conference"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS v FROM "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."g" AS g, "s1"."m1" AS m1, (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS m2 FROM "s1" JOIN "s2" ON "s2"."v" IS NOT NULL), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS v FROM "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."g" AS g, "s3"."m1" AS m1, "s3"."m2" AS m2, ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS m3 FROM "s3" JOIN "s4" ON "s4"."v" IS NOT NULL WHERE "s3"."m2" > "s4"."v") SELECT SUM("s5"."m1") AS m1, AVG("s5"."m2") AS m2, AVG("s5"."m3") AS m3 FROM "s5"
